summary: Frontend visual validation of EUMETSAT Meteosat MSG cloud layer CSS fix. The blur+scale filter is correctly applied and the 'Minecraft' blocky pixel rendering is eliminated on desktop AND mobile.

validation_details.css_class_application: Confirmed: .meteosat-smooth-tile is applied to the Leaflet layer DIV container (parent of 24 WMS tiles). Computed filter='blur(18px) contrast(1.05) brightness(0.94) saturate(1)', transform='matrix(1.04, 0, 0, 1.04, 0, 0)' — exactly matches App.css spec.
validation_details.note_on_request_expectation: The review request expected page.locator('img.meteosat-smooth-tile').count() > 0, but react-leaflet's WMSTileLayer applies className on the layer container DIV (not on each individual ). Filter cascades correctly so the visual fix works. Suggest selector 'div.meteosat-smooth-tile' or '.meteosat-smooth-tile img' in future tests.

desktop_1920x800.clouds_on_visual: Smooth continuous gray cloud mass over the map, NO rectangular pixel blocks visible. Basemap city labels remain readable. Storm cell circles (red/orange/green) clearly visible on top.
desktop_1920x800.zoom_in_x2: Layer remains smooth during and after the Leaflet zoom animation. No blockiness reappears.

mobile_375x812.clouds_on_visual: Smooth cloud overlay, Lourdes label legible, markers visible. No pixelation. User-reported mobile bug confirmed FIXED.

critical_code_review_comments: WeatherLayers.jsx line 167: className on WMSTileLayer is applied to the layer container DIV, not per-tile . Behavior is fine (filter cascades), but worth knowing for future test assertions.

Current CSS solution (blur 18px) is a pragmatic visual hack — long-term consider switching to a higher-resolution Meteosat product (e.g. HRV/visible or RSS rapid scan) if available from EUMETSAT geoserver to avoid the source pixel coarseness at city zoom levels.
context_for_next_testing_agent: CSS fix for Meteosat cloud layer is validated visually on desktop+mobile. If retesting, use selector 'div.meteosat-smooth-tile' instead of 'img.meteosat-smooth-tile' (class is on layer container DIV).
